request: I'm after a little housing for an Arduino Nano, whose board is 45 x 18 mm, to sit on a shelf. It should be possible to get a cable into the Nano's mini-USB port through one of the short ends even with the lid fitted. The lid goes on with snaps rather than screws, so the housing has no fasteners whatsoever, and it carries three 5 mm status LEDs in its top face; they're separate parts wired to the Nano and have to be visible from outside. Because the Nano's header pins point downward and poke out below the board, the board must be held up off the floor. Print the base flat on the bed in PLA without supports. Requirements: Using the Nano from the catalogue, orient it so the mini-USB port looks at one of the short 18 mm ends, put three 5 mm LEDs in the lid, keep the parts from colliding, and state the layout you chose. Inside the closed box the 45 x 18 x 1.6 mm board needs at least 0.5 mm of clearance from every printed surface (its posts excepted), and the USB receptacle has to be within the box. Four posts, no more and no fewer, carry the board, each below a mounting hole and 3.0 to 4.0 mm wide (the hole's own keep-out being 4.0). A locating pin runs through each hole, 0.1 to 0.3 mm under the 1.7 mm hole size, and the header tails must not touch the floor. When the lid is shut, keep everything at least 5.0 mm above the top of the board, and at least 0.3 mm away from the header bodies and pin tails below. With the lid shut, a mini-USB cable has to go all the way into the Nano via one opening in the −X end wall, leaving at least 0.3 mm spare around the plug. Between that opening and the lid seam, the floor and the corners leave 1.5 mm of wall or more. The opening may exceed the plug by 1.5 mm at most per side. Three 5 mm LEDs are carried by the lid: lenses stick out through holes of 5.2 to 5.4 mm in the top face with the flanges held behind, so every dome can be seen from outside and none can be pulled out forwards (flange overlap on the hole of 0.2 mm per side minimum). Put them in a line above the board, spaced 9.0 mm or more apart and 4.0 mm or more from the cavity edge. Only snap hooks hold the lid, with no screws or other fasteners: two or more hooks on each long side and none on the end walls. Hooks are at least 5 mm wide and engage 0.6 to 1.0 mm, on an arm where the bending strain 1.5 t y / L^2 (t thickness, y engagement, L free length) does not exceed 0.02. Make the lid a separate body that sits on the base via a sliding lip, at least 2.0 mm deep with 0.15 to 0.35 mm of clearance each side, and closes flush without the two overlapping. Once closed, the box should have just the USB opening and three LED holes. Wall, floor and lid thickness is 2.0 to 3.0 mm, and every opening has at least 1.5 mm of material around it. Base prints flat on its floor and lid on its outer face, each as a single manifold body needing no supports. Excluding the LED domes, the closed box can be at most 60 x 30 x 26 mm, with its long dimension running along the board's 45 mm side, and it has to stand flat on a shelf and not tip. Hand over a base STL, a lid STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout, and the agent's own clearance report, which has to agree with an independent measurement.
